items.note: S1.1 states that a fixed W-wire linear network exchanges the banks with a sign and restores every scratch wire for arbitrary initial values, which is the conclusion of Lemma lem:scalar-motifs. It omits the formula (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a), the three stages, the eight-row schedule and the triple/neighbour construction, and gives no derivation.

S1.2 carries the mechanism: an invertible frame per vertex commutes with pointwise gates, so only endpoint operators and edge frame changes cost anything (lines 806-825). It does not give the implemented operator D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1} or the route formula eps_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1}.

S1.3a states the comparable nondegenerate labels and the loss of h on central-wire edges, but it drops 'from time 3 to time 4'. The plan never gives L=Ich, the budget Wm-2N+2L or the loss ratios 100/539 and 101/539. S1.3's method only gestures at counting dimension changes, and it misattributes the role of the intersection pairings (see errors).

S1.3b gives total rank s<Wm and endpoint matrix difference I_m on each input role. It omits s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b, the projection assignment P_U with source matrix -P_{U_a}, and the shear frames Phi_M. Nothing shows how the identity or the rank sum follows.

S2.1a correctly states that each edge change is a product of one kernel (aI+bX_v)^{+-1} per orthonormal residual vector, and S2.1b gives C^{otimes e} on every role. The phase frame C_U, the value s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c<W_c m and the source/sink diagonal corrections are absent.

The plan states s<Wm (S1.3b and the S1 motivation) and s/W<m^tau with tau<1 (S1.5). It never gives L<N/2, the deficits eta_b and eta_c, or tau=sigma=1-2^{-50} and its derivation from eta>20*2^{-50} and log m<20.

Only alluded to: S1.4's motivation says controlled shifts update a later field from earlier ones in linear time, and S1.5 splits rows cyclically into W streams. The mod q^b update with a b^{O(1)} offset condition and the list of elementary O(V) operations are not stated.

S1.4a and S1.4b state both lemmas correctly, and S1.4's method follows the paper: triangular parts become linear-time controlled shifts and only the a pivots need interchanges. Two steps are missing: how one pivot addition H_i+=D_j becomes a single interchange (D_j+=H_i, swap, D_j=H_i-D_j; lines 1434-1443), and the elimination proof of the factorization.

The plan follows the paper's route: split rows cyclically into W role streams, run the network with shear frames so that each edge is done by recursive interchanges, three shears with only the middle using the network, s calls on volume V/W, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), F_k=O(e^tau). The fixed-tape depth-first schedule and the W^k row divisibility are not mentioned; they are implementation support rather than route.

S1 and S1.6 state the O(Vu^tau) interchange (p,h,g,d,z)->(p,d,g,h,z) for arbitrary prefix, gap and suffix lengths, and they correctly name row padding and base-m splitting (lines 1684-1706). The high-digit row field and the binary-to-[q^e] padding are not described, so this is not a derivation.

The plan has the edge identity as a product of directional kernels, s_c children on f=e/m axes, and H_0^{otimes D}=b^D S_D C^{otimes D} S_D. It omits the conjugation by P_M that moves residual directions into slot coordinates (eq:phase-edge-coordinate). It also omits the inverse-child identity (C^{-1})^{otimes f}=(-i)^f Z C Z and the reduction of P_M to a fixed number of row additions.

The plan follows the proof: eight rotations that are correct off a guard-defined exceptional set, a bad fraction of at most 80(f-1)2^{-K}, and repair by extraction and radix sort. It states only the simplified cost O(V(L^tau+1)) without the family hypotheses. It never says that each rotation needs chunk swaps, which are the source of the L^tau term (lines 2117-2155), and it omits the separate handling of the top position j_{f-1}.

S2.3 (cyclic row split, children of exactly V/W, padded rows return to zero) and S2.4 (F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1)) match the paper. The unrolling is missing: the leaf cost F(e)=O(e) for e<d^beta, the bound K<=e^{c/beta} that gives overhead O(e^lambda), the base-m pieces, the q_0 row preprocessing, and the condition on lambda'.

S2 and S2.6 state the proposition correctly: one H_0 per chunk at a common offset, exact evaluation then one truncation, O(Vd^{lambda'}), unit disk, error <sqrt2 2^{-p}. The route goes through phase frames, packed additions and the recurrence. The guard width (S2.5) is only asserted: the arithmetic-depth recurrence A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E and the constant C_0 are missing.

The decimation-in-frequency rounds with monomial twiddles, the bit-reversed storage B_t and the reversed procedure are given, and S3.2 states the layout cost correctly. Character cancellation F_t^+F_t^-=t^{-1}I is not stated: S3.1a only calls omega_t a primitive root. The layout permutation L is asserted, not constructed.

The plan follows the paper: evaluation at B_0=2^{4p}, four products by the established multiplier with signs restored, centered residues with carries in {0,1} justified by coefficients below B_0/2, and O(rp log(rp)). The final reduction mod y^r+1 goes unmentioned, but it is routine.

The procedure (retained common LB order, pointwise packed products, opposite transform, exact scale by M) and the error bound sqrt2 M(3l+1)2^{-p} are correct, but the cost bound is not stated. The justification is missing: the record permutation commutes with the pointwise product (P(LBu,LBv)=LB P(u,v)), and the normalization identity.

S4a states the one-dimensional identity with the correct conditions, error and time, and S4b obtains the tensor form gamma=2d alpha^2 by tensoring, as the paper does. The derivation of the one-dimensional resampling identity (lines 3576-3792) is absent.
S5 gives QF_t u = a-bar.(a*(a-bar.u))/T and S6 gives the cancellation of R, both matching the lemma. The chirp's explicit formula and the conjugation remark are not given, and nothing is derived.
The values of b, p, d, K, T, t_i, epsilon, C_1 and kappa, the prime window, and T/2<S<T are correct. Missing: tau, lambda, c, lambda' and delta, eta=1/(4d), alpha, and why the primes exist.

S7.3 says correctly that Phi is an isomorphism preserving cyclic convolution, implemented by triangular controlled shifts and axis moves. It does not give the map x->prod x_i^{mu_i} with mu_i=P_i^{-1} mod s_i, or the triangular digit formula.

The plan follows the paper's derivation exactly: x_d->zeta y is well defined since (zeta y)^r=1, it is diagonal with factor zeta^k, and the wrap check zeta^{k+l}(-1)^h=zeta^j. The resulting formula M_C=D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ f, iota D_+ g) is not displayed.

S7.5-S7.7 give the paper's assembly: the chirp transform, the source transform (A, chirp, B_0, 2^gamma), and the six-step algorithm with the scales S and 2^{2b+4}S. Missing: the digit scaling 2^{-b-2}, and the definition of F^+ by complex conjugation.

The final bound 448b 2^{-3b/4}<1/2, rounding to exact integers, and carries below Q_0^2 are correct. The error chain is missing: the ring and chirp errors, E_s=9 2^gamma TL, E_w<28 2^gamma T^2 L, and gamma<=b/4.

Normalization by V=Tp, min g_i=2^{-181}=2kappa from the chunk-exchange term, absorption of log powers, and the final O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}) all match the paper. Only two of the seven table rows (simultaneous rounds and Gaussian lines) appear, and the seven powers and margins are not listed.
S0 names the integer-multiplication conjecture as a dependency, but no step says that one machine with T_A(n)/(n lg n)->0 negates the eventual lower bound.

errors.says: Method: attach subspaces built from triple indicator vectors, 'using their intersection pairings to cancel unwanted gather and scatter coefficients'.
errors.paper: The scalar network itself cancels the unwanted gather/scatter coefficients, through side injection (lines 752-759). The labels use the intersection pairing for a different purpose: neighbouring triple lines are orthogonal, so side-wire labels nest, P x <t_X> in P x t_Y^perp (lines 861-870, 946-953, 1048-1055).

errors.says: The labels are chosen 'so that ... every route has endpoint difference the identity'.
errors.paper: The endpoint identity comes from the rational matrices assigned on top of the labels: P_U at gates and sinks, -P_{U_a} at sources X_a, zero elsewhere. That gives P_{U_a^perp}+P_{U_a}=I_m (lines 1115-1118, 1169-1171). Labels alone do not give it.

errors.says: Only the central-wire edges lose dimension, by h each.
errors.paper: Only the central-wire edges from time 3 to time 4 decrease. The other central edges (source->1, 1->3, 4->6) increase or are flat (lines 998-999, 1031-1034).

chain: The tree follows the paper's architecture: interchange via the bit network (S1), the simultaneous layer via phase frames (S2), synthetic ring convolution (S3), resampling/chirp/cancellation (S4-S6), the algorithm and exact recovery (S7), and cost accounting (S8), ending at O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}). It thins out at the central saving. The plan asserts s<Wm and s/W<m^tau, but the dimension budget Wm-2N+2L, rank equals dimension change, L/N<1/2 and tau=1-2^{-50} are all missing, so the power saving is claimed rather than reconstructed. The guard-width depth recurrence, the error chain in exact recovery, and most of the cost table are likewise only asserted.

steps.note: S1.1 describes a fixed W-wire network exchanging two banks with a sign and restoring scratch wires, and S1.3 mentions three-element subsets. Missing: h=100, triple-indexed banks, N=C(h,3)^3, m=h^3, and the explicit (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a).

S1.2 gives the mechanism: an invertible frame per vertex commutes with pointwise gates, so only the endpoint operator and each edge's change of frame cost anything. The formula D_out S D_in^{-1} is implied rather than written.

Nondegenerate subspaces of an m-dimensional space built from triple indicators, comparable on every edge, only central-wire edges decreasing by h. The plan omits that the decrease is only on the 3->4 edge, and it omits the F^{otimes3} structure.
The plan speaks of 'counting dimension changes' and of 'the sum s of the edge ranks' but never says that rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U. The N rank-one source exceptions are also absent.
No budget formula appears: Wm-2N+2L, L=Ich and s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b are all missing. Only the method phrase 'count the dimension changes along edges' points to it.
s<Wm is stated, but L/N=100/539 (101/539), L<N/2 and the deficit N-2L>0 that produces it are absent.

S1.3b gives endpoint matrix difference I_m on each input role. S1.4c has the middle shear H<-H+D done by the network, which is the shear that identity produces on every role. The projection assignment that yields it is not given.
Rank-a shear factored as E_1 Pi E_2, costing exactly a interchanges plus O(V), with s recursive calls per node in total.

The recurrence part is complete: children of volume V/W, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), and s/W<m^tau giving F_k=O(e^tau). But tau=1-2^{-50} and its justification from eta>20*2^{-50} and log m<20 are absent. Since half the step's defining content is missing, the verdict is conservatively 'mentioned'.

central.summary: The plan reconstructs the frame principle, the labels, the endpoint identity and the edge-as-recursive-calls step, along with the form of the recurrence. The quantitative core of the saving is missing: rank equals dimension change, the budget Wm-2N+2L, L/N<1/2 and the explicit tau=1-2^{-50}. So s<Wm and s/W<m^tau appear as asserted conclusions rather than as a reconstructed chain.
